newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian bank merger outlook unchanged-analysts.
newsitem.headline: Australian bank merger outlook unchanged-analysts.

text.p: Australia's fifth largest bank, St George Bank Ltd, said on Monday that it had no comment on a newspaper report it was again examining takeover options after recent comments from the anti-monopolies body.

Analysts also told Reuters that comments from Alan Fels, the chairman of the Australian Competition and Consumer Commission (ACCC), did not justify speculation that the industry was suddenly on the verge of more takeover activity.
Even so, the shares of St George had risen sharply by the end of morning trade in response to the report.
The Sydney Morning Herald newspaper said St George could be considering a bid for the Bank of Queensland Ltd.
St George shares were 20 cents higher at A$8.73 at 12.30 p.m.(0230 GMT) but in moderate turnover of 500,000.
But in Brisbane, Bank of Queensland Ltd said it had no comment on the speculation about a St George Bank.
"We don't dont make comment on unsourced speculation and a rumour," Bank of Queensland chairman Neil Roberts told Reuters.

Analysts said the banks and finance groups such as St George, Colonial Ltd, Bank of Queensland and the Bank of Adelaide Ltd which were potential targets prior to Fels' comments at a news conference last Friday and in a Sunday television interview, remained so.
Little could be gleaned from his recent opinions that the regulatory environment had changed, they said.

The Herald said St George's corporate advisers were working on various scenarios for a possible bid for Bank of Queensland, even though that bank is 44.5 percent owned by the Queensland government which has not said it was a willing seller.
But on directions from Federal Treasury, the government has to sell down its stake to under 10 percent in three years.
"I have every expectation there will be discussions with the state government in due course as to the ultimate destination of the shares to be sold," Roberts said.

Fels, who last Friday approved the A$1.44 billion takeover of regional operation Bank of Melbourne Ltd by Westpac Banking Corp, said he would probably not be troubled by a St George bid for Bank of Queensland.

Fels held a news conference and television interview to discuss his rulings on the Westpac bid, which followed months of negotiation to retain the Melbourne bank's identity, and the regulator's view of the role of regional banks in the industry.
Shares in Westpac Banking Corp were also much higher, with a gain of 26 cents to a 1997 high of A$8.49.
"I guess you could argue that if Westpac was benefitting from mergers and acquisitions then perhaps St George will as well," said one insitutional broker.
"Anything smaller than ANZ has got to be a target," said the broker.
"The local market is difficult to grow. The only way you can grow market share is to accumulate assets from other sources even though it may not be the best use of capital."

Whereas Westpac is considered a "Big Four" bank due to its national branch system and mix of business and residential lending, others such as Bank of Melbourne and St George are considered "regional banks" because of their limited geographic coverage and their heavy reliance on home lending.
Prior to last Friday's ruling, the ACCC had opposed takeovers of regional banks by major banks, citing the need for each state to have its own regional bank operation.
Australia's largest bank in terms of assets and profits, National Australia Bank Ltd, is also the largest shareholder in St George with a 5.54 percent stake.

NAB views its stake as strategic but analysts said it could not move against St George without support from the target's board of directors due to the restrictive articles of association which limits individual holdings to 10 percent.

In comments which helped spark renewed industry takeover talk, Fels said on Sunday that he would look at any NAB bid for St George on its merits but pointed to likely concerns with potentially excessive market share in South Australia.
